key_insight: Pulsed electric fields enable programmable droplet generation in a T-junction by controlling interface motion, wall contact, and breakup timing.
engineering_relevance: Electrode placement and pulse timing offer design controls for microfluidic systems requiring tunable, consecutive droplet production.
method: Simulate two-phase flow using the phase-field lattice Boltzmann method.
Compare no-field, top-biased, and bottom-biased electrode configurations.
Analyze filling and squeezing stages and map droplet regimes across pulse parameters.
evidence_signal: Simulations show electrode-dependent interface evolution, while droplet sequence diagrams and regime maps demonstrate sensitivity to pulse parameters.
watch_item: The abstract reports numerical results without experimental validation; practical performance may depend on accurately reproducing wall wetting and contact-line pinning.
paper_title: Droplet formation dynamics in a T-junction via pulsed electrohydrodynamics
